issues.description: revoke_error exposed to API without sanitization, access gating, or defined schema
issues.detail: The PR author explicitly asks in the description whether revoke_error is safe to expose. It is a free-form stringified error that may contain backend URLs, hostnames, or credential fragments. Either gate behind sudo/root, strip to a coarse status, or define a typed shape (code + message). Do not ship a field whose own author flags it as potentially sensitive.

issues.description: leaseInfoForExport conflates redaction policy with field selection via ad-hoc struct literal
issues.detail: The function is the trust boundary deciding what leaves the expiration manager, but the allowlist is an implicit struct literal anyone can extend in one line. Express the exported field set as explicit data with a documented redaction contract (what is included, what is omitted, why) so security review has one auditable place to look.

issues.description: Test coverage for new fields is one assertion on path; namespace_path and revoke_error untested
issues.detail: Tests assert only path == 'secret/foo'. The two genuinely new conditional behaviors — namespace_path inclusion when a namespace exists, and revoke_error inclusion when set — have no coverage of either branch. Add cases that exercise present and absent for each, so the API contract is locked by tests rather than prose.

issues.description: Metric label 'expire.fetch-lease-times' was not updated alongside the function rename
issues.detail: The defer metrics.MeasureSince call still uses the old key after renaming FetchLeaseTimes to FetchLeaseInfo. Keeping the metric stable to avoid breaking dashboards is defensible, but the decision should be a comment. Otherwise the next renamer will 'fix' it and break operator alerts, or the name silently becomes a lie.

issues.description: Response shape mixes conditional and unconditional fields inconsistently
issues.detail: handleLeaseLookup emits path unconditionally but omits namespace_path and revoke_error when empty. Pick one convention — always-present-with-zero-value or omit-when-empty — across all three new fields. Mixed conventions in one response object cause clients to grow special cases. A small descriptor for field/source/condition would make the contract auditable.

issues.description: Schema marks path Required:true but code does not enforce non-empty and historical entries may be empty
issues.detail: Required:true on the new path response field is a compatibility claim the code does not back up — leaseInfo.Path is whatever was stored, and old leases may have empty path. Either drop Required, or assert non-empty in code. Do not lie in the schema.

synthesis.summary: A small, mostly mechanical rename (FetchLeaseTimes -> FetchLeaseInfo, leaseTimesForExport -> leaseInfoForExport) plus three new exported fields on lease lookup: path, namespace_path, revoke_error. The panel agrees the rename itself is honest but the new surface area is under-audited. The dominant concern: revoke_error is shipped as an opaque string with the PR author openly asking whether it is safe to expose — that question must be answered before merge, not after. The redaction boundary (leaseInfoForExport) is expressed as an implicit struct literal rather than an explicit allowlist, and test coverage exercises only the easy path field while skipping the two conditional branches that were actually added. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK — resolve the revoke_error policy, make the export contract explicit, and cover the new branches.
